extracted.intended_audience: high school contestants, coaches, team leaders, and organizers involved in Chinese national mathematical competitions and IMO preparation
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the structure, scoring, selection procedures, and organizational responsibilities for China national mathematics competitions (China Mathematical Competition, CMO, China Western/Girls' MO) and procedures at the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO). Useful for contestants, coaches, and competition organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: China Mathematical Competition — paper structure and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The test paper consists of 6 choices, 6 blanks and 3 questions to be solved with complete process. The full score is 150 marks. Besides, 3 questions are used in the Extra Test, with 50 marks each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants with high total marks in the China Mathematical Competition plus the Extra Test are awarded the first prize (about 1,000 participants around China), and they will be admitted into the university directly. Excellent marks in this competition are used to select students to take part in the China Mathematical Olympiad the next year.

rubrics_metrics.name: China Mathematical Olympiad (CMO) — format and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: CMO (Winter Camp) lasts for five days; the types and difficulty of the problems match those of IMO. Participants solve three problems every day in four and a half hours each day. Starting from 1990 each problem is scored out of 21 marks (total 126).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMO awards first, second and third prizes. From CMO about 20 to 30 students are selected to participate in national training for IMO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection pipeline for China's IMO team
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection proceeds from China Mathematical Competition (≈200,000 participants) → about 120 students selected to CMO → about 20–30 students selected for national training → after 6–8 tests plus two qualifying examinations, six students are selected to form the national IMO team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training for the national team typically lasts two weeks in March each year; CMO is held in January; China Mathematical Competition is held in October; IMO occurs in July.

rubrics_metrics.name: China Western Mathematical Olympiad & China Girls' Mathematical Olympiad — selection rule
rubrics_metrics.description: China Western Mathematical Olympiad (started 2001) and China Girls' Mathematical Olympiad (started 2002) provide routes into national selection: the top two winners of each are admitted directly to the national training team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specialized competitions aim to promote participation from western regions and encourage more female students to join mathematical competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMO — contest format and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: IMO test paper consists of 6 questions given over 2 days (3 questions each day) with total contest time of 9 hours. Each question has 7 marks (total per contestant 42 marks); full team score is 252 marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately half of participants receive medals, with the numbers of gold, silver and bronze medals roughly in the ratio 1:2:3; if a participant provides a better solution than the official answer, a special award is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and problem submission rules at IMO
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating country must send a delegation consisting of a leader, a deputy leader, and 6 contestants. Problems are contributed by participating countries; the host country prepares a shortlist of submitted problems for the international jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The host country does not provide any question. Short-listed problems are translated into working languages, and team leaders translate them into their own languages for their teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury, marking coordinators, and dispute resolution at IMO
rubrics_metrics.description: Team leaders initially mark their contestants' scripts and present them to coordinators. Coordinators assess and the jury (team leaders + appointed chairman) finalizes marking standards and resolves disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jury responsibilities include finalizing marking standards, ensuring translation accuracy, standardizing replies to written queries during the competition, synchronizing marking differences between leaders and coordinators, and deciding medal cut-off points depending on problem difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking accuracy and fairness mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Host countries nominate coordinators; coordinators and a group of mathematicians serve to ensure high accuracy and fairness in marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: China formed a group of 50 mathematicians as coordinators when hosting the IMO to ensure accurate and fair marking; the marking process may be completed earlier if efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem difficulty standard for national selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems in CMO and selection tests are designed to match the difficulty and type of IMO problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and training tests emulate IMO format (three problems per 4.5-hour session, similar difficulty) so that students are prepared for international standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of the China Mathematical Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives: to increase students' interest in learning mathematics, promote development of co-curricular mathematical activities, help improve teaching of mathematics in high schools, discover and cultivate talents, and prepare for IMO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competition functions as the first step toward IMO selection and historically has large participation (around 200,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewards and progression criteria from national contests
rubrics_metrics.description: High total marks across the China Mathematical Competition and its Extra Test determine award of first prize and direct university admission; excellent performance selects students for CMO and further training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Extra Test consists of 3 problems each worth 50 marks; combined scoring determines top awardees and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team championship and prizes at CMO
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting 1990, the Chern Shiing-Shen Cup was instituted for team championship at the Winter Camp (CMO); CMO was officially named in 1991.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team performance is recognized via this cup and team awards are part of the CMO structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics that guide problem-setting for IMO/CMO
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical topics include number theory, inequalities, graph theory, polynomials, functional equations, complex numbers, combinatorics, geometry and game theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subject areas guide problem setters and indicate the content scope candidates should prepare for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal cut-off and difficulty-dependent scoring policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury decides cut-off points for medals depending on the difficulties of problems each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because problem difficulty varies annually, medal thresholds are adjusted by the jury rather than fixed absolute scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation accuracy and standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations of shortlisted problems into working languages (English, French, German, Russian, etc.) are prepared; team leaders translate into their own languages. The jury ensures accuracy of translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring accurate translation is a jury responsibility to avoid misinterpretation and coordinate standardized replies to queries during the exam.
